headline: Lagarde Says AI Has Helped Europe Withstand Higher Energy Prices
author: Jorge Valero

paragraphs.text: Thu, November 26, 2026 at 3:59 AM PST 2 min read
(Bloomberg) -- European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said artificial intelligence is one factor helping the region weather the energy crisis, according to people familiar with the matter.

She told European leaders in Brussels on Thursday that the economy has seen more resilience than anticipated to the fallout from the Iran war, the people said, asking not to be identified because the discussion was confidential.

Lagarde said that AI and energy are among three forces shaping the outlook, with the other being the increase in global long-term interest rates, they said. While that phenomenon is partly a reflection of expectations for higher central-bank borrowing costs, the main driver has been largescale issuance of bonds from governments and companies, the people cited her saying.
The ECB president also urged leaders to ensure that legislation for the digital euro is completed before the end of 2026, according to the people.

Lagarde is set to leave her post on Feb. 7, almost nine months before her term concludes. Leaders are also discussing her succession, with Spaniard Pablo Hernandez de Cos the clear favorite for the job now that France and Germany have agreed on his candidacy.
"I believe that by the end of the day we will know for certain who will take over this key role in Frankfurt," Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic told reporters on his way into the meeting.
